key_insight: Cluster-TNN scales topological deep learning by lifting graphs locally inside mini-batches instead of materializing the full higher-order domain upfront.
engineering_relevance: This makes higher-order neural networks practical on large, dense graphs by cutting GPU memory sharply while preserving competitive accuracy.
method: Partition the input graph during preprocessing.
Sample groups of clusters at runtime and reconstruct their induced subgraphs as mini-batches.
Apply the chosen lifting operation within each mini-batch while retaining all edges among sampled nodes.
evidence_signal: Across 21 matched comparisons with full-graph training, Cluster-TNN reduced peak GPU memory in every case, averaging 83.2% savings and enabling training on Reddit and OGBN Products.
watch_item: Because the method relies on cluster partitioning and local reconstruction, performance may depend on partition quality and on whether the sampled mini-batches preserve enough higher-order connectivity.
paper_title: Batch Before You Lift: Scalable Topological Deep Learning on Large Graphs
